canonicalExplanation.summary: **Contrast ratio** compares the lightness of two colours, from 1:1 (identical) to 21:1 (black on white). WCAG asks for at least **4.5:1** for normal text, **3:1** for large text, and **3:1** for meaningful UI parts like input borders and **focus indicators**. A colour that passes on white may fail on grey, over a photo or on a translucent panel — so measure it on **every background it can appear on**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your error text is `#e11d48` — it passes on the white form. But the same error also appears on the grey card and the dark header, and the orange focus ring sits right on an orange button. The design file only showed the white case. A focus indicator and error text are measured on every background they can overlap, not only the design canvas. In this lesson you'll measure and repair text, component and focus-indicator contrast.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Lengths, percentages and viewport units**, **Paragraph and inline meaning**, **Custom properties and design tokens**, and **Readable text metrics**.

sections.heading: The rule: minimum ratios, measured in context
Don't rely on colour alone

includes: Measure contrast for text, UI components and focus indicators against every background they meet.
Repair failures using tokens and never rely on colour alone.
excludes: APCA and future contrast methods in depth.

outcomes: Measure and repair text, component and focus-indicator contrast.

examples.title: Measuring focus and error colours everywhere
examples.situation: A focus indicator and error text are measured on every background they can overlap, not only the design canvas.
walkthrough: **List backgrounds:** error text appears on white, #f3f4f6 cards, and the dark #111827 header.
**Measure each:** #e11d48 passes on white (4.7:1) but only 4.3:1 on #f3f4f6 and 3.8:1 on #111827 — two failures. The orange focus ring on an orange button is ~1.2:1.
**Repair:** use #b91c1c on light backgrounds and #fca5a5 on the dark header; change the focus token to #1d4ed8 with a 3px offset, then measure again.
examples.result: Error text and focus rings meet their ratios on every background they can overlap.

examples.title: Text over a hero photo
examples.situation: White headline text sits on a sunset photo. It's readable on the dark sky, invisible over the bright sun.
walkthrough: The worst spot (white on yellow) is about 1.1:1.
Fix: add a dark translucent overlay or a solid panel behind the text, then measure against the lightest area under it.
examples.result: The headline meets 4.5:1 over every part of the photo it covers.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A contrast-safe text hex value remains compliant on every translucent or image background.
misconceptions.correction: Contrast depends on both colours. A value that passes on white can fail on grey, dark, translucent or photographic backgrounds. Measure against every background where the text or indicator can appear.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Measuring focus and error colours everywhere", on which backgrounds did the original error colour fail?

analogy.example: Contrast is like **a sign's readability at night and day**: the same letters can be clear on a white board and invisible on a grey wall. You check the sign everywhere it's hung, not just in the print shop.
usefulFor: remembering contrast is a pair, not a colour
limitations: Signs have fixed backgrounds; web components move between them.
Focus rings are like signs that appear only when you point at something.

artifact: focus ring orange on an orange button

steps.explanation: Error text is measured on every background it can overlap.
The focus indicator is measured against what it sits next to.

remediation.explanation: For each colour, write down **every background it can appear on** (including hover, dark mode, photos). Measure each pair. Any below its minimum gets a new token value.
remediation.retryPrompt: Do this for "Text over a hero photo".

recap.summary: To measure and repair text, component and focus-indicator contrast, check 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text, UI parts and focus rings — against every background they meet — fix failures in your tokens, and never rely on colour alone to convey meaning.
